summary.text: 女 is a whole-figure pictograph of a woman, commonly interpreted in early forms as kneeling or seated with her hands crossed or engaged in an activity.

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph depicts a woman as a whole figure. The kneeling or seated posture is an interpretation of early forms; accounts differ about the position of the hands.

components.text: The whole graph depicts a woman. Early forms are interpreted as a kneeling or seated figure with hands crossed or engaged in an activity; it is not split into smaller parts.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as a kneeling or seated woman. Later bronze forms simplify the seated posture, and one account says the depiction had become difficult to recognize by the Warring States period. These are changes in written form, not evidence of a change in meaning.
A proposal that the modern form is reversed from oracle-bone forms, with strokes representing a breast, remains uncertain. Descriptions of the figure’s posture and hands also differ.

uncertainties.text: The specific posture and hand position in the early figure are not described uniformly. The proposed reversal and breast interpretation of the modern form are not confirmed by the other cited accounts.
Early inscription accounts report several uses of 女 beyond ‘woman’, but their dates and contexts do not establish whether each was a borrowed spelling or a meaning development.

senses.text: Early inscription accounts report female-related uses, while the Han-period Shuowen glosses 女 as ‘woman’. The specific inscription examples are not dated here, so this is the earliest documented sense in these accounts, not proof of the graph’s original meaning or priority among early uses.
Early inscription accounts report 女 used for 母, including cited oracle-bone examples. This establishes an early use or overlap, but not a semantic development from ‘woman’.

senses.gloss: reported uses for 毋, 每/悔, 汝, 如, and place names
senses.text: Inscription accounts report these uses of the graph. They may include spellings borrowed for other words, but the available accounts do not give enough context or sound evidence to explain each use.

A separate lexical reading is recorded with the meaning ‘give as a wife’. The supplied historical readings distinguish it from 女 ‘female’, but do not date this use or establish how the meanings are related.
Dictionary and definition records list these meanings, but do not establish when they arose or how they developed from ‘woman’.

limitations.text: The reported uses and dictionary glosses do not establish dated transitions among these meanings, so no semantic-development links are asserted.

overview.text: 女 is a picture of a woman, interpreted in early forms as a kneeling or seated figure. Later changes to its shape do not by themselves show a change in meaning.

components.text: Read the whole graph as a woman; early forms are interpreted as a kneeling or seated figure.
